subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity next steps

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity next steps

Hi Alice / Ravi - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

TL;DR: Redwood will run a focused model-fit evaluation against your proprietary baseline using your prompt sets and a small labeled holdout. We'll surface performance on accuracy, instruction-following, hallucination rate, latency, and cost.

Recap from the call:
- Business goal: extract and normalize payment metadata (payer, amount, invoice_id, remittance_note) from semi-structured payment confirmations; target throughput ~75 req/s peak.
- Success criteria: parity w/ proprietary model on key QA metrics (we discussed 95% relative F1 on critical fields) and tolerable hallucination regression (<=3% absolute increase).
- Constraints: data residency in us-east-1; limited labeled set (~1,200 examples) and larger unlabeled set for sampling.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) You to share the prompt sets and a representative test sample (anonymized) - push to the Drive folder you mentioned or send a link.
2) Redwood to run an initial parity eval (open models vs your baseline) with recommended candidates: Llama-3-13B-8k-qlora, Mistral-7B-Instruct-quant, and our tuned Redwood-11B-lite (quantized) as the fallback. We'll include cost/latency estimates per 1k requests.
3) We'll deliver a short parity report (pdf) + raw benchmark CSV and recommended next steps within 5 business days of receiving the test set.
4) Schedule a 30-min kickoff to walk through the test data and acceptance thresholds - Calendly link below.

Attachments: paygrid-initial-benchmarks.xlsx (ciphered sample of metrics template we'll populate).

Questions for you now:
- Can you confirm the acceptance threshold discussed (95% relative F1 on payer/amount/invoice_id) and the allowable hallucination delta (<=3% absolute)?
- Will the test set include edge cases we flagged (multi-invoice emails, non-USD currency formats)?

Thanks - I'll coordinate internally once you confirm.

-- Lauren

- Acceptance thresholds: confirmed - our internal baseline target is as you wrote: 95% relative F1 on payer/amount/invoice_id for the primary cohort. Hallucination / false-positive tolerance: we can accept up to a 3% absolute increase but would like recommendations if any model exceeds that.
- Test set: we will upload an anonymized 1,250-example labeled CSV that includes the edge cases (multi-invoice, non-USD, legacy HTML receipts).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PayGrid eval plan & recommended models

Lauren / Aditya - thanks for the invite. I pulled the prompt sets and initial sample from the Drive link Alice shared. High-level technical plan and recommendations below.

Plan:
- Phase 1: Small-scale parity eval (1,250 labeled examples) across 3 candidate models + PayGrid baseline (they provided baseline metrics). Measure: field-level F1, exact-match for critical fields, hallucination rate (false entities per 100 responses), token cost, median latency (p50) at batch size 1 and simulated 75 req/s throughput.
- Phase 2: If Phase 1 meets parity thresholds, run 5k sample stress test with KV caching/prefix caching enabled to estimate cost savings and latency under load.

Model selection rationale (candidates):
1) Llama-3-13B-8k-qlora (open, instruction tuned) - good balance of instruction-following and cost; initial benchmarks often near 92-97% of larger proprietary baselines on structured-extraction tasks.
2) Mistral-7B-Instruct-quant - cheaper inference cost, sometimes stronger on instruction-following with quality similar to 13B class on many commercial tasks.
3) Redwood-11B-lite (quant. 4-bit) - our internal tuned variant; slightly higher cost than Mistral but often more consistent on hallucination-sensitive tasks.

Acceptance criteria suggestion (to align with Sales / Customer asks):
- Primary: >=95% relative F1 on payer/amount/invoice_id compared to PayGrid baseline.
- Hallucination: <=3% absolute increase in false entities per 100 responses.
- Latency/Cost: per-1k-request token cost no more than 60% over their current baseline for acceptable models; otherwise provide mitigations (batching, caching).

Quality regression concerns / caveats:
- Small labeled set (1.25k) is workable but may underrepresent rare edge cases; recommend PayGrid provide at least ~200 labeled examples of multi-invoice and currency-edge cases if possible.
- Tokenization differences and table-like HTML can cause field-splitting issues; include a normalization step in our eval harness to avoid penalizing correct extractions with formatting differences.

Deliverables for Phase 1 (ETA 5 business days once we have sample):
- PDF parity report (open-vs-prop-parity-report-20270418.pdf)
- Raw CSV benchmarks and dashboards (paygrid-initial-benchmarks.xlsx)
- Prompts & eval harness artifacts (prompt-sets-paygrid-v1.jsonl)

I'll run the initial eval on a small dedicated pool to keep latency stable and attach the results. If anything looks off on hallucination, we'll try Redwood-11B-lite with conservative decoding params and rerun.

On the Calendly timing - I can do Thursday 10:30 PT to walk through the test set and acceptance criteria.

-- Marissa
